title: Effect of Oxygen Concentration on Corrosion Mechanisms of 316L in Liquid <mark>Sodium</mark> at 550 °C
abstract: Oxygen is a known corrosion accelerator in sodium-cooled fast reactors; however, published studies have primarily used <mark>sodium</mark> containing no oxygen, saturated oxygen, or one single oxygen concentration and explored the effect of varying temperatures and operating conditions. In this study, we investigate the effect of increasing oxygen concentration on the corrosion behavior of 316L austenitic stainless steel in a static testing environment at 550 °C for 100 h.
